title: Russia Bombards 9 Ukrainian Cities Overnight; 2 Killed, 14+ Wounded
detail: Russia launched a 'massive' overnight combined strike on nine Ukrainian cities using ballistic missiles (Iskander-M/KN-23), Onyx anti-ship missiles, S-8000 Banderol strike drones, and roughly 258 Shahed-type/decoy drones, with the barrage running from Wednesday night into Thursday morning, August 27. Ukraine's Air Force said it shot down or suppressed 1 Onyx missile, 7 Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles, 3 Banderol drones, and 222 of the attack drones. Four districts of Kyiv were hit, damaging a sports complex in Pecherskyi district, an educational facility in Shevchenkivskyi district, a medical facility, and sparking a vehicle fire in Holosiivskyi district; no fatalities were reported in the capital. Elsewhere, a 78-year-old woman was killed in Zaporizhzhia region and one person was killed in Kherson region, with at least 14 people wounded nationwide. Russian drones destroyed toy-store and confectionery distribution warehouses in Kyiv region, four glide bombs knocked out generating equipment at Kherson's combined heat and power plant, and Odesa was attacked for over 7 hours, damaging a 16-story residential building, two schools, and a grain elevator.

title: Ukraine Missiles Strike Russian Main and Reserve Command Posts Near Donetsk
detail: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Russian occupiers' main and reserve command posts near occupied Donetsk with air-launched cruise missiles on August 26, into the overnight and morning of August 27, per the General Staff. Targets reportedly included an underground parking area of an unfinished residential complex and the buildings of the former UkrStateNDIplastmas research institute; OSINT monitor Exilenova+ assessed one site may have housed the command post of Russia's 51st Guards Combined Arms Army. The General Staff said it was still assessing damage and losses. The same operation also struck a repair-and-restoration unit near Chongar (Kherson region), a UAV control post at Olenivka (occupied Crimea), and concentrations of Russian personnel near Novopetrivka (Zaporizhzhia region) and Voskhod (occupied Crimea).
